context: Set 2 of 3 — branch disposition, the standards fork, and the two reporting defects that make fleet counts wrong. Marathon run mrun-20d9230f767b. Evidence tables at claude.ai/code/artifact/77dcfcf1.

questions.question: You ruled on 2026-08-23 that 067-qr-link-provisioning graduates to its own /bk-specify pipeline. That settles what the feature does next but not what happens to the existing branches: origin/067 is 26 commits ahead with 3 conflicts and origin/067b is 27 ahead with 4. Meanwhile the roadmap still carries the feature at state 'implemented'. A feature that is 'implemented' and also 'go specify it from scratch' is a contradiction. What happens to the 53 commits?
blocks: 2 of the 5 remaining unmerged origin heads

options.label: Merge both, then specify
options.means: Resolve the 7 conflicts, merge both branches to develop, then write the new spec against a real codebase. Also move the roadmap row off 'implemented' so table and pipeline agree.
options.cost: Seven conflicts across two branches is a bounded but real afternoon, and the new spec inherits code it did not author.

options.label: Archive both, re-implement
options.means: Archive-tag and drop both branches; the new pipeline re-implements from the spec.
options.cost: Discards 53 commits the roadmap itself calls implemented, and this line's private-key history makes any later re-merge harder, not easier.

options.label: Defer to the new plan
options.means: Leave both branches open until the new feature's /bk-plan decides what to salvage.
options.cost: Keeps 2 of 5 unmerged heads alive indefinitely — exactly the state the Y-series exists to exit.

questions.question: Merging olamnit's branch produced an add/add conflict on scripts/roadmap_open_table.py, and BOTH files cite your 2026-08-23 ruling: develop carries 9798 B ('BK-STD-1 section 2, proposed by ariellas-tefl'), itself the product of an earlier withdrawal, and olamnit carries 11295 B ('FLEET STANDARD', adopted from qhstate d1f64b4). I kept develop's, deleted nothing and picked no winner, because unilateral picking is how the last fork started. Which is canonical?
blocks: the fix for the dropped-state defect below

options.label: olamnit's qhstate-derived file
options.means: Adopt olamnit's as canonical fleet-wide; develop replaces its copy; ariellas-tefl's is withdrawn explicitly.
options.cost: Against my own repo's file, and it carries 1497 B of behaviour I have not diffed. A larger file is not automatically the better one.

options.label: develop's BK-STD-1 file
options.means: develop's stays canonical; olamnit withdraws theirs.
options.cost: Keeps the standard living in one repo's scripts/ with no external lineage — which is the condition under which it forked twice already.

options.label: Diff and merge the superset
options.means: Compare both, publish one file carrying both lineages and any behaviour unique to either.
options.cost: Loses nothing but costs a real comparison plus another round of fleet agreement before anyone can quote a number.

questions.question: The fleet-standard open table drops state='implemented'. Measured on today's export: 119 features = 94 closed + 15 promoted + 6 specified + 3 analyzed + 1 implemented, so 25 are not-closed — but the renderer prints 24. The hidden row is qr-link-provisioning (067), the feature carrying an open engineer ruling. Separately, epic heads carry NO state field at all, so no lane can support an epic state count. How should not-closed be defined and rendered?

options.label: Render implemented as not-closed
options.means: Treat implemented as not-closed and render it, in whichever file the fork question makes canonical. Correct by the plain meaning of not-closed.
options.cost: Every lane's published count changes by its implemented rows — a visible correction that must be announced, not slipped in.

options.label: Exclude it, footnote it
options.means: Keep implemented excluded by design, but print the exclusion in the mandatory footer so no reader can miss it.
options.cost: A table headed 'not closed' that omits a not-closed state stays misleading at a glance, however well footnoted.

options.label: Add epic state, render both
options.means: Extend the export so epics carry state, and render epics and features in one table — the only option that makes 'all epics and features not closed' literally answerable.
options.cost: Requires an export schema change and fleet-wide re-export before any lane's table is comparable again.

questions.question: The marathon's own next pointer names a step that cannot run: 082-feature-stream-superset has no feature_pipeline row (21 rows, 082 absent) so /bk-clarify is default-denied, and starting it would take the single active slot from 078, which has held it 11.9 days at WSJF rank 1. 082's code merged to develop on 2026-08-20 while its roadmap row stayed 'promoted', and whether it folds or is scoped as the engine half has been undecided since 08-23. Which is it?

options.label: Fold 082 into the hardening feature
options.means: Fold 082 into scheduler-feature-stream-durable-healing-and-hardening, close its roadmap row as folded, and retire the blocked step.
options.cost: Ends 082 as a separately trackable feature, so its specific scope survives only inside the parent's spec.

options.label: Scope it as the engine half
options.means: Give 082 its own pipeline row and clarify it after 078 closes.
options.cost: Waits on 078 regardless, and keeps a roadmap row and pipeline slot open for code that already landed four days ago.

options.label: Leave it, re-point the step
options.means: Change nothing on 082; just re-point the marathon's next step at 078's own work.
options.cost: The resume pointer keeps naming an impossible step, which is the same false-green class that 078 exists to eliminate.
